comment: Seam audit round 4, finding 9. One sidecar_identity (key-bearing) component, one chain state, two gates that must agree:
the Store's promote and serve gate (verifySidecarClassComponentOnChain; sidecar_identity_key_version_parity_test.go) and
the tenant update controller's apply gate (cmd/melusina-update-controller gateSidecarCascade;
cmd/melusina-update-controller/sidecar_identity_key_version_parity_test.go). Both read this file and must give each case
the same verdict, refused by the same name. A refusal is matched as a substring of the error; an empty refusal means the
Every chain fact comes from the contracts repository's committed sidecar PDA vector, the byte-for-byte copy at
testdata/contracts/sidecar-pda-vectors.json (vector contractsVector): its program, master, reseller and licence mints,
sidecar id, and the Global, Reseller and Local approval addresses. identityPda 'kv1' and 'kv2' are that vector's
expected SidecarIdentityEntry addresses for key versions 1 and 2. 'kv0' is the key-version-0 address; the vector does
not carry it, because no program phase registers key version 0, so each consumer derives it with its own code.
The chain holds exactly one SidecarIdentityEntry, Active and pinning the artifact, at registeredKeyVersion: the only
key version the contracts tenant phase registers (scripts/estate/lib/tenant-sidecar-authorization.mjs
keyVersion 0 is what an omitted keyVersion decodes to (the field is omitempty); each consumer asserts the component's
JSON carries no keyVersion key in that case, so 'omitted' is what is refused.
componentId and artifact name the one component both gates see: its sha256 is sha256(artifact) as UTF-8 bytes, the
Global approval and the registered identity pin that hash, and every other chain field comes from the contracts vector.
